rows.scenario: Baseline: label decoded with the issuer's registry entry and contexts
rows.outcome: proof valid: true

rows.scenario: Signed label after a routine vocabulary update (one term added under the same URL)
rows.outcome: label UNREADABLE: decode error "Improperly formatted bytes <payload bytes> found."; the reason (codec drift) is not reported, and the label stays unusable for its lifetime

rows.scenario: Compact profile signing the CBOR-LD bytes, after the same update
rows.outcome: signature valid: true; meaning changed silently; graph: dataAccessScope = battery#RestrictedData

rows.scenario: Registry entry substituted at the verifier (context codes swapped)
rows.outcome: decode error: Unknown term ID "180" was detected in the CBOR-LD input.

rows.scenario: M15 v0.4, WE-2 label (I-RDFC); verifier's context was updated; no archive
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch: the verifier's inputs for registry entry 100 do not reproduce the bound digest, and the issuer's manifest is not in the archive, so the differing input cannot be named

rows.scenario: M15 v0.4, WE-2 label (I-RDFC) + lifetime archive of the issuer's manifest and material
rows.outcome: ACCEPTED (I-RDFC, lifetime archive (resolved by manifest digest)); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#PublicData

rows.scenario: M15 v0.4, WE-2 label (I-RDFC); registry entry substituted at the verifier; issuer's manifest published
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch: type table "context": https://contexts.example/energy-roles/v1 is 32769 at the issuer, 32768 at the verifier; type table "context": https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2 is 32768 at the issuer, 32769 at the verifier; the archive holds the issuer's manifest but not its material

rows.scenario: Profile B (issuer signs the envelope), honest round trip
rows.outcome: ACCEPTED (B, local registry); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#PublicData

rows.scenario: Profile I-RDFC (inner ecdsa-rdfc-2019 proof), honest round trip
rows.outcome: ACCEPTED (I-RDFC, local registry); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#PublicData

rows.scenario: X4: profile A (signature over CBOR-LD bytes only), envelope rewritten to match a verifier with the updated context
rows.outcome: REJECTED at policy: profile A rejected by policy: its signature covers only the CBOR-LD bytes, so the registry entry id and manifest digest can be rewritten to match a drifted verifier (X4). If A were accepted: signature valid: true; ACCEPTED (A, local registry); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#RestrictedData

rows.scenario: X4 against profile B: the same rewrite
rows.outcome: REJECTED at signature: envelope signature invalid for did:key:zDnaezpMR3RpByA12JifUfWjK84YgsM4kbhmSgsNCaHSjTUN1#zDnaezpMR3RpByA12JifUfWjK84YgsM4kbhmSgsNCaHSjTUN1 (profile B)

rows.scenario: X8: profile I-JCS (inner ecdsa-jcs-2019 proof), envelope rewritten to match a verifier with the substituted context
rows.outcome: REJECTED at policy: profile I-JCS rejected by policy: an ecdsa-jcs-2019 inner proof binds the JSON, not the RDF graph, so a rewritten envelope can decode into another meaning under a valid proof (X8). If I-JCS were accepted: inner JCS proof valid; ACCEPTED (I-JCS, local registry); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#RestrictedData

rows.scenario: X8 against profile I-RDFC: the same rewrite
rows.outcome: REJECTED at inner-proof: inner ecdsa-rdfc-2019 proof invalid with the pinned inputs (signature)

rows.scenario: X7 with the v0.3 manifest scope: profile B over a top-level manifest; imported context substituted; unpinned decoding
rows.outcome: signature valid: true; top-level contexts match; decodes; graph: dataAccessScope = battery#RestrictedData

rows.scenario: X7 with v0.4 (transitive manifest, profile B); imported context substituted; no archive
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch: the verifier's inputs for registry entry 100 do not reproduce the bound digest, and the issuer's manifest is not in the archive, so the differing input cannot be named

rows.scenario: X7 with v0.4; issuer's manifest published, material not archived
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch: context https://contexts.example/battery-scopes/v1: the verifier's bytes (sha384-mchJMzoXGB+g…) differ from the issuer's (sha384-We59d6Uy53Kg…); the archive holds the issuer's manifest but not its material

rows.scenario: X7 with v0.4 + lifetime archive of the issuer's material
rows.outcome: ACCEPTED (B, lifetime archive (resolved by manifest digest)); graph: dataAccessScope = battery#PublicData

rows.scenario: v0.4 decoder given a signed top-level manifest (v0.3 scope); verifier holds the issuer's bytes
rows.outcome: REJECTED at decode: undeclared URL requested during decoding: https://contexts.example/battery-scopes/v1 (not in the decoding manifest)

rows.scenario: Decoder drift (MC-4): profile B; verifier's decoder reports version 9.0.0 (simulated); archive holds the issuer's material
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch that the archive cannot repair: decoder: the issuer used @digitalbazaar/cborld 8.1.0, the verifier runs @digitalbazaar/cborld 9.0.0

rows.scenario: Codec drift under an unchanged version string: verifier's build adds a URL codec (simulated)
rows.outcome: REJECTED at manifest: decoding manifest mismatch that the archive cannot repair: codec semantics differ: urlCodecs
